For any element X we use the usual bracket notation

 [X/H] = log10[(nX / nH)star] – log10[(nX / nH)☉]  
 [X/Y] = log10[(nX / nY)star] – log10[(nX / nY)☉].

1.  Silicon abundance in Star 1  
   We are given  
 [Fe/H]₁ = 0 and [Si/Fe]₁ = +0.3.  
   Therefore  
 [Si/H]₁ = [Si/Fe]₁ + [Fe/H]₁ = +0.3 dex.  
   Hence  
 log10(nSi/nH)₁ = log10(nSi/nH)☉ + 0.3.

2.  Silicon abundance in Star 2  
   For Star 2 the data are  
 [Mg/H]₂ = 0 and [Mg/Si]₂ = +0.3.  
   First write [Mg/Si]₂:  
 [Mg/Si]₂ = log10(nMg/nSi)₂ – log10(nMg/nSi)☉ = +0.3.

   Because [Mg/H]₂ = 0, Mg has the solar abundance in Star 2, so  
 log10(nMg/nH)₂ = log10(nMg/nH)☉ = –5.

   Let S = log10(nSi/nH)☉ (its exact value is not needed).  
   Then log10(nMg/nSi)☉ = log10(nMg/nH)☉ – log10(nSi/nH)☉ = –5 – S.

   For Star 2:  
 log10(nMg/nSi)₂ = –5 – log10(nSi/nH)₂  
        = (–5 – S) + 0.3   (from [Mg/Si]₂ = +0.3).

   Hence  
 –5 – log10(nSi/nH)₂ = –5 – S + 0.3  
 ⇒ log10(nSi/nH)₂ = S – 0.3.

   Thus [Si/H]₂ = log10(nSi/nH)₂ – S = –0.3 dex.

3.  Ratio of silicon abundances  
   Difference in [Si/H] between the two stars:  
 [Si/H]₁ – [Si/H]₂ = (+0.3) – (–0.3) = +0.6 dex.

   A difference of +0.6 dex corresponds to a factor  
 10^{0.6} ≈ 3.98.

Therefore the number ratio of silicon atoms in Star 1 to those in Star 2 is about 4, i.e. ~3.9.
